claim_text: Spotify had a login outage on the morning of Tuesday, Nov 24, that logged many users out and stopped them signing back in
summary: From about 6:15 AM ET on Nov 24, many Spotify users in several countries were logged out and could not sign back in. TechRadar's reporter was logged out of the iOS app and could not log back in.
detail: TechRadar saw the problem first-hand. Numerama, Digit and RIA Novosti each read Downdetector's report counts and describe mostly login failures, with some app and playback problems. Some users were asked to set up a new account instead of signing in. Numerama says offline downloads could still play if the session had not been closed.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: A first-hand check by one outlet and separate report-tracker readings by three more outlets agree on the outage.

claim_text: Downdetector showed more than 16,500 reports in the US and more than 8,000 in the UK at the peak
summary: TechRadar reported over 16,500 Downdetector reports in the US and over 8,000 in the UK at about 6:58 AM ET. Digit gives a US peak of 16,451 against a baseline of eight.
detail: These are user-submitted reports, not a count of affected users. We did not read Downdetector ourselves. Digit's peak times are in India time.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets relay Downdetector's counts and agree on the US peak.

claim_text: Users in at least a dozen countries reported problems, mostly with logging in
summary: RIA Novosti lists Downdetector reports from the US (10,600), Germany (6,100), the UK (4,600), the Netherlands (2,700), Italy (1,900) and other countries. Numerama counts 2,000+ in France; Digit about 800 in India.
detail: Counts were taken at different times by each outlet, so they do not add up. Digit says about 70% of US reports were about logging in; Sunday Guardian gives 68%; Numerama, citing the tracker Instatus, gives 61% at the peak.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Several outlets read user-report trackers in different countries.

claim_text: Spotify's status account said it was aware of issues and was checking them out
summary: Spotify's official status account on X posted: "We're aware of some issues right now and are checking them out!" TechRadar and Numerama both show the post.
detail: TechRadar logged the post at about 7:00 AM ET. It is Spotify's only statement on the problem that we found, and it gives no cause. Numerama says Spotify's status page showed no incident; we did not use that page.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Two independent outlets each show Spotify's own post.
notes: The post is on a social platform; the outlets are cited for it.

claim_text: Sign-ins were working again by about 7:15 AM ET
summary: TechRadar posted at about 7:15 AM ET that its reporter, and many others on Downdetector, could sign in again. Numerama says Spotify's status account later posted "Everything's looking much better now."
detail: The outage lasted roughly an hour by TechRadar's account. Spotify has not said the problem is fully fixed or given an end time. Digit said servers were returning to normal.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's first-hand check and one outlet's report of a Spotify post; Spotify has not given an end time.

claim_text: The cause of the Nov 24 login outage
summary: Spotify has not said what caused the outage. No source we read gives a cause.
detail: TechRadar, Numerama and Digit each say Spotify had not explained the problem. Numerama's update says the company gave no explanation of where the outage came from.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Three outlets report that Spotify gave no cause.

claim_text: No source we read says the Spotify outage was a cyberattack, or rules one out
summary: We found no claim of responsibility, no DDoS claim, no report of an attack and no Spotify statement on the cause. We also found no statement ruling an attack out. Being logged out is not by itself a sign of a hack.
detail: A search for a hack or DDoS claim about Spotify on Nov 24 found none. None of the five outlets mentions an attack.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources gives a cause or mentions an attack.

claim_text: The start time differs between sources, from about 6:15 to 6:34 AM ET
summary: TechRadar says problems started at about 6:15 AM ET. Numerama says US problems began at 6:34 AM ET, and RIA Novosti says complaints began about 2:32 PM Moscow time (6:32 AM ET).
detail: The outlets read report trackers at different times; the difference is small and does not change the finding.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Three outlets give close but different start times.
